title: Compact distance-preserving cabinet contact geometry
coverage_gap: The support remains just one LL and one HH demonstration. Development feedback now shows A1 at 20/20 C and 20/20 E, A2 at 20/20 C and 19/20 E, and A3 at 20/20 C and 6/20 E. No A1 failure mechanism was observed. A4 therefore tests whether A1's redundant coordinates can be removed while preserving its successful physical bias and reducing conditioning cost; it does not invent a failure-specific repair.
reusable_regularity: A compact contact-and-motion tuple plus cabinet orientation and world anchors determines the physically present raw state. Keep explicitly useful nonlinear contact/goal distances, but remove alternate coordinates that are exactly derivable. This favors direct metric relations over a larger collection of correlated geometric views. Cabinet-aligned translation actions, quaternion sign invariance and fixed physical scales are retained from A1. Stage discovery remains learned entirely by the common DP.
dependencies_preserved: World hand position, world goal position and cabinet sin/cos remain direct conditioning channels; fixed robot orientation, workspace anisotropy and cabinet obstacle placement are not marginalized out.

The local current hand-handle and goal-handle vectors and local hand/handle increments retain all current/native-previous position information. Given world goal g and cabinet R, o=g-R*v_goal; h and native previous h/o are recoverable from retained relations and increments. World h is also explicitly retained rather than requiring this reconstruction.

Both current and native-previous handle orientations remain as first/third rotation columns in the cabinet frame. Both apertures remain. Contact and goal distances remain explicit for stage discrimination. Both whole causal observations are used.
Goal/handle/hand heights and the obstacle's cabinet yaw are preserved. No fitted hinge, new sensor, simulator state, planner or oracle is introduced. The absent object2 zero fields remain omitted.

evidence_refs.use: Same exact two support episodes; no extra support in revision.
Causal raw field layout, observed yaw, native world action semantics and fixed end-effector orientation.
Only LL/HH support, near-constant cabinet cosine, and matching initial handle-goal length motivate retained metric cabinet geometry rather than empirical yaw normalization.
Above-handle alignment: retain the scalar contact distance and vertical component rather than dropping all derived phase-relevant invariants.
Contact and opening motivate retaining causal handle/hand increments.
Large changing handle orientation while cabinet/world remain fixed: preserve both pose history and world anchors.
Native previous fields are sufficient to form explicit velocity and contact relations without a trajectory-time input.

evidence_refs.source: revision message development_feedback and q3 record_selection
evidence_refs.use: Frozen scores A1=1.000, A2=0.975, A3=0.650 select A1. A1 latency 0.1032762465 s and 4746820 parameters motivate a compact revision at the observed success ceiling. A2 has one E-LL native truncation; A3 has fourteen E truncations. Aggregate feedback does not localize contact failures and multiple design differences prevent attributing the contrast to auxiliary loss alone.

evidence_refs.source: frozen A1 candidate authored in this session
evidence_refs.use: Actual implementation parent: retain action frame, physical scales and geometric dependencies; ablate ten redundant conditioning channels.

expected_failure_signature: If redundant world relative vectors were crucial for the DP to compensate world-fixed gripper/control-cube effects, A4 may lose large-yaw E success while keeping C success. Information equivalence does not guarantee equally easy learning from N=2.
If the extra previous-contact or aperture-difference features eased optimization, removing them may worsen descent/opening timing despite retaining the underlying current/previous quantities.
A4 may preserve success but not improve measured inference latency: the fixed U-Net sampling loop dominates cost, so fewer features do not guarantee a faster fixed-method measurement.
Even matching A1's finite development success would not establish universal robustness; each C/E distribution has only twenty development episodes.

required_runtime_fields.source: Only causal_context.raw_history [B,2,41] and raw_current [B,41], with fixed configuration-derived metric scales. Common normalized history is accepted but raw metric geometry is used.
required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Identical semantics to A1: encode the native xyz vector by Rz(cabinet_yaw_at_chunk_start)^T, decode by Rz from that same causal context for all 16 steps. No translation, gain, gripper rotation, local clipping or future-frame conditioning. Native xyz units stay 0.01 m per unit; gripper retains [a3,-a3] control semantics. Only the host clips after decoding and executes four actions.
required_runtime_fields.conditioning: 36 features per observation: 12 contact/goal/motion vector components, 12 current/native-previous pose column components, 2 apertures, 2 scalar distances, and 8 explicit world hand/goal/yaw components. No learned encoder, phase gate, time counter or deployment state cache.

support_fit: None; empty deployment-state dictionary. Fixed metric scale buffers are created only in build_modules from the same config as A1. There are no stored examples or support-fitted constants.
architecture: One unchanged common factory DP at condition_dim=36 and diffusion_action_dim=4, retrained from the public seeded initialization for the full fixed budget. The U-Net internals, optimizer, horizon, noise schedule and common epsilon action loss are unchanged. There is no auxiliary loss and no checkpoint/weight reuse from A1.
change_summary: Revision after the single permitted A1-A3 feedback round; q3 recorded as A1 by the frozen C/E rule, not IID or training loss.

Reduce conditioning dimension 46->36. Remove native-previous local hand-handle vector (3), explicit aperture difference (1), and duplicate world hand-handle/goal-handle vectors (6). Keep all source physical dependencies, explicit distances, full pose history and world anchors.

The removed previous-contact vector equals current contact minus hand increment plus handle increment in the same cabinet frame; aperture difference is derivable from the two apertures; world vectors are inverse rotations of retained local vectors.

Vectorize the eight cabinet-frame vector transforms and the two quaternion-to-column conversions in one batched computation. This is an implementation/conditioning efficiency change, not a change in control semantics.

Do not import A2's support-fitted circle/phase experts or A3's graph/joint future-state channels. Their feedback informs parsimony but does not prove any one component harmful. A1-A3 remain immutable; A4 is one fresh scientific training slot.
